title: The Lyra Technique II: SVD Denoising and Persona Intensity in KV-Cache Geometry
subtitle: Version 1.2 (2026-11-20): the selection-bias finding is scoped to the 45 scale-sweep cells it tested, so the persona and emotion denoising gains are untested upper bounds. Version 1.1 (2026-11-01): the W_K emotion channel is corrected at source and withdrawn as a reading of model or user state
abstract: Version 1.2, corrected 2026-11-20 (version 1.1: corrected 2026-11-01). The emotion channel this paper reported as W_K directional projection is corrected at source: the probe applied no W_K (it was a class-mean key readout), and its labels are the emotion a generator was asked to write into a third-person story, not the user's or the model's state. On 30 classes it scores 0.410 against a text (TF-IDF) baseline's 0.370 (Holm p = 0.071, not significant; 0.348 with FWL fitted on the training fold), and the method as described scores 0.358 against 0.382. The binary AUROC 0.992 beats text (0.963, Holm p = 0.006), but on ten emotions (n = 300), confounded with arousal; the injection test is withdrawn. Raw spectral features detect confabulation at AUROC 0.663-0.913 across a 15-model scale sweep; a within-model deception result (AUROC 1.000) is retracted, since the same-prompt control collapses it to 0.160. SVD denoising was tested as an amplifier. Across the 45 model-by-task cells of the scale sweep (confabulation and self-reference tasks), 0 of 16 positive denoising deltas exceed a max-over-rank selection envelope, so those gains are indistinguishable from selection noise. The apparent persona gains (AUROC 0.611-0.751 raw, 0.899-0.992 denoised) and the denoised emotion result were not part of that analysis: they are untested, and their denoised values are upper bounds pending a pre-registered rank criterion. The raw AUROCs are the defensible numbers. That dominant singular values carry scale and residual values carry discriminative structure is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated tool.
